title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Automating Spark Upgrades with Codex Agents at OpenAI
gist: At QCon San Francisco 2026, OpenAI data infrastructure manager Mouli Mukherjee described using Codex-driven agents to automate Spark upgrades across an exabyte-scale platform with millions of cores, arguing agents belong in open-ended operational work while deterministic systems (shadow runs, config overrides, validation) provide the guarantees agents operate within.

insights.claim: OpenAI's Mouli Mukherjee argues AI agents are most useful not for rebuilding a data platform but for open-ended operational work that is hard to turn into fixed playbooks, such as debugging where failure modes cannot be enumerated in advance.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Points to platform operations (not platform replacement) as the near-term enterprise market for agents.
insights.locator: At QCon San Francisco 2026, Mouli Mukherjee

insights.claim: Mukherjee holds that anything requiring consistent outputs for the same inputs — access control, configuration resolution, data correctness guarantees — should stay in deterministic systems, which agents use as tools rather than reimplement.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Agent adoption increases, rather than replaces, demand for deterministic infrastructure and guardrail tooling.
insights.quote: We should definitely build the systems where we want guarantees and guardrails.
insights.locator: Mukherjee clearly distinguished between deterministic systems and agents

insights.claim: OpenAI's data platform runs at exabyte scale with hundreds of thousands of datasets and a Spark fleet on millions of cores.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Indicates the size of AI labs' data-infrastructure footprint beyond GPUs.
insights.locator: OpenAI's platform runs at exabyte scale

insights.claim: Before letting Codex agents upgrade Spark jobs, OpenAI built a shadow-run service reusing production inputs on a low-priority queue, a configuration override service to stop experiments changing global settings, and a validation skill comparing production and shadow runs.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: A replicable blueprint for safely deploying agents on production infrastructure.
insights.locator: The Spark upgrade outlines steps taken to ensure safety

insights.claim: Once safeguards were in place, OpenAI's agents claimed jobs, launched shadow runs, reviewed validation reports, classified errors and moved jobs to the new Spark version.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Agents are already doing end-to-end migration work at a frontier lab, an adoption signal for Codex.
insights.locator: After these safeguards were in place

insights.claim: For lower-risk incremental library releases OpenAI sometimes skips the shadow step and promotes directly, trading capacity for higher rollback risk, while jobs that pass shadow validation but later fail in production auto-roll back to the previous Spark version.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Shows explicit cost/risk trade-offs in agent-driven operations.

insights.claim: OpenAI's agents now continuously tune Spark job efficiency by inspecting query plans, trying config changes, comparing runs and iterating.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Agent-driven compute optimisation could lower data-infrastructure costs.
insights.locator: Agents can tune job efficiency continuously

insights.claim: On the support side at OpenAI, agents search past incident reports, suggest runbook updates, trace stale tables through orchestrator and scheduler logs, and explain access-control denials, while permissions still enforce the user's own credentials.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Agent-assisted platform support is a near-term target for internal tooling budgets.

insights.claim: Mukherjee recommends starting agents on repetitive, open-ended tasks where judgment matters, building safety mechanisms first, and only then letting agents operate inside those bounds so experimentation stays repeatable, observable and reversible.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Adoption playbook that favours vendors of observability, sandboxing and rollback tooling.
insights.locator: Mukherjee recommended starting with the repetitive
